# Codegen

`@softistx/limix-codegen` turns three inputs into one TypeScript file that
registers them in `@softistx/limix`: the REST operations (an OpenAPI document),
the GraphQL operations (SDL files or the schema graphql-codegen holds) and the
names a rules file uses. Core's `Register` interface reads the file by module
augmentation, so `definePolicy` and `compilePolicy` check against it.

## The generated file

```ts
// Generated by @softistx/limix-codegen from schema.graphql, openapi.yaml, rules.yaml.
// Do not edit: run `limix-codegen generate` again (`--check` in CI).

export type LimixRest =
	| 'GET /notes'
	| 'GET /notes/:id'
	| 'DELETE /notes/:id';
export type LimixGraphql = 'Mutation.createNote' | 'Note.body' | 'Query.me';
export type LimixPermission = 'notes:read' | 'notes:write';
export type LimixRole = 'admin';
export type LimixCondition = 'workingHours';

declare module '@softistx/limix' {
	interface Register {
		rest: LimixRest;
		graphql: LimixGraphql;
		permission: LimixPermission;
		role: LimixRole;
		condition: LimixCondition;
	}
}
```

Commit it, and keep it inside your tsconfig `include`: the augmentation works
only when the file is in the program. The output is sorted (REST by path, then
method; the rest by code unit), LF, with a fixed header, so the same inputs
always give the same bytes.

## What each key checks

| Key | Source | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rest` | `--openapi` | `definePolicy`: a path key must be a path of the API, and a method under it a method the API declares on that path |
| `graphql` | `--graphql` or the plugin | `definePolicy`: a type and a field must exist in the schema, on every type (roots and others) |
| `condition` | `--rules` | `compilePolicy(rules, { conditions })`: a name the rules file does not use is refused; a name it does use may still be missing (a runtime `RulesError`) |
| `permission`, `role` | `--rules` | Nothing in core: `Permission` and `Role` give your own code the unions |

## What stays unchecked

- A key whose input was not given: without `--graphql`, GraphQL rules accept any
  type and field.
- A path key holding `*` or `{`: `/files/*path` and `/a{/:b}` name several
  routes and are accepted with any method.
- Rule bodies: `permissions`, `roles` and `when` inside `definePolicy` are not
  narrowed, since that would make the rules file depend on its own generated
  types. `canOf` and `holdsPermission` stay `string`, so graxia's `can` stays
  assignable.
- `HEAD` is registered only when the spec declares it.
- A rules file loaded with `loadRules`, or any rules that do not go through
  `definePolicy`: the types see only the literal you write in code.

## OpenAPI conversion

Keys are written without `global.basePath`; `servers` and Swagger 2 `basePath`
are ignored. Both OpenAPI 3.x and Swagger 2.0 are read, from `.yaml`, `.yml` or
`.json`. A path item that is a `$ref` is refused: bundle the spec first.

| OpenAPI | Rules file |
| --- | --- |
| `/notes/{id}` | `/notes/:id` |
| `/files/{id}.json` | `/files/:id.json` |
| `/files/{id}x` | `/files/:"id"x` (the name would run into the text) |
| `/files/{file-id}` | `/files/:"file-id"` (not an identifier) |
| `/a(b)` | `/a\(b\)` |
| `/a:b*` | `/a\:b\*` |

Each of `get put post delete options head patch trace query` under a path item
becomes an operation. `parameters`, `summary`, `description`, `servers`, `x-*`,
`additionalOperations` and `webhooks` are ignored.

## A starter rules file

```sh
limix-codegen init --openapi openapi.yaml --graphql schema.graphql
```

writes `rules.yaml` (`--rules` picks another name; `.json` writes JSON): every
REST operation and every GraphQL root field gets `authenticated: true` under
`unmatched: deny`. Only root fields are listed. The file is validated and
compiled before it is written. `init` never rewrites an existing file (it
exits 0 with a notice), so follow up with coverage, which lists what is new:

```ts
import { coverage } from '@softistx/limix/coverage'
import { openapiOperations } from '@softistx/limix-codegen'
import { graphqlOperations } from '@softistx/limix-graxia/operations'

coverage(policy, [...openapiOperations(doc), ...graphqlOperations(sdl)])
```

## The graphql-codegen plugin

```ts
export default {
  schema: 'schema.graphql',
  generates: {
    'src/generated/limix.ts': {
      plugins: ['@softistx/limix-codegen/graphql-codegen'],
      config: { rules: 'rules.yaml', openapi: 'openapi.yaml' },
    },
  },
}
```

`rules` is one file, `openapi` one file or a list. The plugin needs no
`@graphql-codegen/plugin-helpers`. It reads files through Bun, so start it with
`bun --bun graphql-codegen`, and it relies on the one copy of `graphql` that
graphql-codegen uses. It writes its own output file: GraphQL comes from the
schema, so the header names `the GraphQL schema`. graphql-codegen's own
`--check` compares that file the way it compares any other.
